newsitem.title: UK: Pills fogged my brain, Britain's Fergie says.
newsitem.headline: Pills fogged my brain, Britain's Fergie says.

text.p: Britain's Duchess of York on Sunday blamed some slimming pills taken when she was a teenager for fogging her brain and diminishing her judgment.
The duchess, known familiarly as "Fergie" after her maiden name Sarah Ferguson, said she underwent a personality change after taking the pills while on a visit to her mother in Argentina.
"I was only on them for about four days. But I can tell you now...I feel that it certainly added a bit of fog and confusion to my mind," she told BBC television.
Fergie, divorced last May from Prince Andrew, Queen Elizabeth's second son, described how she felt at 16, gawky and square next to the slender and chic Argentine women.
"One of my friends said to me "look, try these new injections and these new slimming pills'," she told comedienne interviewer Ruby Wax.
"What I realise now is that suddenly, I got changed into another person."
Fergie said she attacked her mother Susan, who had been divorced from her father and was married to Argentinian polo player Hector Barrantes.
"I don't know whether it made me crazy but all I can tell you is, I got so angry with Mum I nearly drew a knife on her," she said.
"I feel that it certainly added a bit of confusion to my mind...I think this is what we call toxins and I think that was what stayed in my system."
The 37-year-old duchess, always frank about her struggles with her weight, said she had cleansed her system recently with a drink made of asparagus, spinach, watercress and celery juices.
Adding to revelations and self-flagellation made in a series of interviews to promote her autobiography, the duchess said she had been her own worst enemy.
She described the incident in France in 1992 when she was shown cavorting with "financial adviser" John Bryan. The photographers, she said, were luckier than they had hoped for.
"They never dreamt that I would take my top off and be kissed on the foot by a bald chap. They lucked out," she said.
"I really did a good job... Talk about kicking myself in the shin. It's a wonder I didn't break my leg."
Earlier, Fergie said Bryan had beaten her black and blue in a fit of rage after she refused to show him her diary.
The duchess told The Independent on Sunday the attack happened in March 1995 after a dinner party.
"I wouldn't let him look at it. He hit me. I had bruises all down my arms because I held them up to defend myself," she told the newspaper.
The duchess said she still loved Prince Andrew and added that the queen was one of the few members of the royal family who had shown her kindness.
